title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap, and retrospective (Q1 2026)
author: Rohit Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the Platform team’s authoritative systems & services inventory, standard dashboards and alerting rules, runbooks for common incidents, a short how-to section for oncall engineers, Q1 2026 retrospective findings, and the roadmap for platform reliability and observability work in 2026. It is intended for oncall engineers, platform owners, and program managers.

Goals
- Provide a single reference for service owners and oncall responders.
- Standardize alert thresholds and response actions to reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM).
- Drive roadmap priorities based on Q1 retros and capacity projections.

Systems & Services Inventory (summary)
- platform-api: public REST/GRPC gateway for Redwood API. Owner: platform-api-service team. SLO: 99.95% availability; p95 latency <120ms for text-generation routes.
- routing-service: request routing and smart model selection. Owner: runtime-routing. SLO: 99.9% availability; p95 latency <80ms.
- batch-service: background batching and prefetch for embeddings and long-running jobs. Owner: batch-team. SLO: throughput target 2000 r/s sustained for reserved pools.
- kv-cache: distributed prefix/KV cache used by serving runtime. Owner: serving-runtime. SLO: cache hit-rate >85% for steady-state workloads.
- metrics-ingest: Prometheus remote-write + metrics pipeline. Owner: observability. SLO: 99.9% ingestion success (90th percentile).
- gpu-scheduler: capacity manager for Dedicated pools. Owner: infra-capacity. SLO: allocation latency <30s for autoscale events.

Dashboards and Alerts (standardized)
Dashboards (canonical):
1) Platform Overview (Grafana): service availability, global request rate, 1/5/15m error rates, p50/p95/p99 latency by route, token spend by model, and autoscale events timeline.
2) Serving Runtime Health: kv-cache hit-rate, GPU memory pressure, KV cache eviction rate, live model sizes, and decoder throughput.
3) Dedicated Capacity & Scheduler: pool utilization, allocation latency, pending queue length, and spillover to burst capacity.
4) Metrics Pipeline: remote-write success, sample cardinality, and pipeline lag.

Key alert rules (severity mapping below):
- P0 (page): platform-api error rate >= 1% sustained for 5m OR platform-api availability < 99% for 10m.
- P0: GPU node OOM or GPU driver crash reported in last 2m on >= 2 nodes in same AZ.
- P1 (pager optional): p95 latency for production text-generation routes > 300ms for 10m.
- P1: kv-cache hit-rate < 60% for 15m.
- P2 (ticket): pending batching queue > 1000 requests for 5m.
- P2: metrics-ingest pipeline lag > 3m for more than 10m.

Severity definitions and oncall expectations:
- P0: Immediate page to primary oncall + 15-minute bridge if not acknowledged. Pager duty escalation: primary > secondary > oncall-lead.
- P1: Slack alert + page for oncall if sustained > 15m. Triage within 30 minutes.
- P2: Create ticket and assign to owner within 24 hours.

Example PromQL alert (for p95 latency):
  
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="platform-api",env=~"prod"}[5m])) by (le, route)) > 0.3

Runbooks (top incidents)
1) High error rate on platform-api (P0) - Steps:
  1. Acknowledge page and join bridge.
  2. Check recent deploys: `git log --oneline origin/main..origin/prod` and the deployment dashboard (link on Dashboard page).
  3. Run: `kubectl get pods -n platform-api -o wide` to identify CrashLoop or OOM.
  4. If a deploy is suspect, rollback to previous stable image: `kubectl -n platform-api set image deployment/platform-api platform-api=registry.redwood-inference.com/platform-api:stable-20260201` and monitor.
  5. If error rates persist and logs show model loading failures, check routing-service health and kv-cache: `curl -s http://routing-service.prod.svc/health` and `curl -s http://kv-cache.prod.svc/stats`.
  6. For database-related errors, contact infra-database and enable read-only mode for non-critical jobs.
  7. Post-incident: create a postmortem per the incident process and link it to this page.

2) GPU node failures (P0) - Steps:
  1. Identify affected nodes: `kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, conditions:.status.conditions}'`
  2. Drain node(s): `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and check autoscaler behavior.
  3. If driver crash, redeploy nvidia-driver-daemonset: `kubectl rollout restart ds/nvidia-driver -n kube-system`.
  4. If OOM caused by model, consider evicting largest pods or scaling out pool. Use `gpu-scheduler` to request extra nodes: `rgctl allocate --pool dedicated-gpu --count 2` (internal CLI).
  5. If multiple AZs are impacted, enable fallback routing to Hosted tier (temporary). Notify SRE and infra-capacity.

3) kv-cache degradation (P1) - Steps:
  1. Check cache hit-rate metric < 60% and eviction rate.
  2. Restart cache pods one at a time: `kubectl -n serving-runtime rollout restart sts/kv-cache` and monitor hit-rate.
  3. If cause is load spike, increase cache memory for the statefulset and adjust eviction policy (see appendix config table).

How-tos (common tasks)
- Adding a new Grafana panel: duplicate an existing panel from the Platform Overview dashboard, update the PromQL query, and add ownership metadata in the panel description (owner: team-slug).
- Creating a new alert rule: create in Alertmanager via the Alerting UI, include runbook link, owner, severity, and escalation policy. Test in staging for 48h before enabling in prod.
- Onboarding a new service to SLOs: complete the SLO intake form (link) and add metrics to the `service_slo` dashboard. Monitor for 14 days to establish baseline.

Retrospective — Q1 2026 (summary)
Successes:
- Reduced mean cold-start latency for small models by 18% after kernel selection improvements in runtime (Feb 2026).
- Improved autoscaler stability: allocation failures decreased by 40% after scheduling backoff logic fixes.

What went wrong:
- Two P0 incidents in Jan related to model-loading races when multiple large models were pinned by different customers to the same Dedicated pool. Root cause: concurrent eviction and disk pressure.
- Observability gaps: some synthetic check coverage for multi-tenant Dedicated pools was missing and resulted in delayed detection.

Action items (owner — ETA):
1. Add pre-checks for concurrent model pin operations and prevent overlapping heavy pin ops (owner: serving-runtime, ETA: 2026-04-15).
2. Expand synthetic checks to include Dedicated pool model-load scenarios (owner: observability, ETA: 2026-05-01).
3. Create an operational guardrail: limit concurrent model-streaming loads per node to 3 (owner: infra-capacity, ETA: 2026-04-01).

Roadmap (Q2–Q4 2026 highlights)
Q2 2026:
- Deliver model pinning pre-checks and rollout in Dedicated clusters.
- Add autoscale dry-run mode to preview allocation decisions in staging.
Q3 2026:
- Implement tiered alert suppression for scheduled maintenance windows and rollout windows.
- Begin migration of metrics-ingest to a partitioned remote-write cluster to reduce tail latencies.
Q4 2026:
- Launch per-customer capacity planning UI in Console for Dedicated customers.
- Introduce predictive scaling for burst workloads driven by traffic patterns and eval-run forecasts.

Appendix: Config table (kv-cache recommended tuning)
| setting | recommended value | rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| cache.memory_limit | 64Gi | baseline for 4-node pool serving large models |
| eviction.policy | lru-ttl | reduces long-tail eviction churn |
| eviction.target_hit | 0.85 | target steady-state hit-rate |

Appendix: useful commands & links
- Grafana dashboards: /grafana/d/PLATFORM_OVERVIEW
- PagerDuty oncall rota: https://pagerduty.com/org/redwood-oncall
- SLO intake form: /confluence/eng-platform/slo-intake-form
- Internal CLI docs: /internal/rgctl/docs

Post-incident process reminder
- For every P0/P1 incident created in the last 90 days, ensure a postmortem is filed and linked to this page within 7 days. Use the incident template and tag owners.
